description: A finance director must authorize a one-time share repurchase and set its amount, execution method, tax reserve, and filing timetable, with input from treasury, legal, and tax accounting.

shared_context.S1: The company has proposed a one-time share repurchase before the end of the fiscal quarter.
shared_context.S2: The preliminary proposal describes a $5,000,000 repurchase but does not finalize the execution method, tax reserve, or filing timetable.
shared_context.S3: Elena makes the binding capital-allocation decision.
shared_context.S4: At the capital-allocation meeting, Elena routinely asks treasury, legal, and tax accounting to report any relevant conditions before she signs the authorization.

PF1.text: Marcus confirmed in this morning's rolling cash forecast that exactly $4,200,000 is the authorized repurchase amount that can be paid while preserving the board-approved operating cash floor. This $4,200,000 is the repurchase amount itself, not a total pool from which the tax reserve should be deducted; the excise-tax reserve is booked separately. The updated forecast has not yet been circulated.

PF2.text: Nadia found in the current board resolution while reviewing the corporate records this week that the repurchase must be conducted through a Dutch auction and may not use an open-market program; she has not yet updated the draft authorization.

PF3.text: Jonah confirmed in a tax memo received yesterday that the repurchase requires an excise-tax reserve of exactly $126,000 and a tax filing within 30 days after execution; the memo has not yet been added to the transaction file.

acceptance_conditions: The repurchase must be approved for exactly $4,200,000.
The repurchase must use a Dutch auction.
An excise-tax reserve of exactly $126,000 must be recorded.
The tax filing must be scheduled within 30 days after execution.
The authorization must include a commitment implementing the Dutch-auction execution requirement.
The authorization must include a commitment implementing the $126,000 excise-tax reserve and 30-day filing requirement.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'dutch_auction_execution' or c['type'] == 'execution_method' or c['type'] == 'execution_method_constraint' or c['type'] == 'dutch_auction' or 'Dutch auction' in c['detail'] or 'dutch_auction' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'excise_tax_filing' or c['type'] == 'tax_filing' or c['type'] == 'tax_reserve_and_filing' or ('$126,000' in c['detail'] and '30 days' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The preliminary proposal names $5,000,000 without confirming the authorized amount; PF1 changes repurchase_amount_usd to exactly $4,200,000, clarifies that the tax reserve is separate from that amount, and supports approval at that amount.
The preliminary proposal leaves execution_method open; PF2 changes execution_method to Dutch auction and requires a commitment implementing that method.

The preliminary proposal has no tax treatment; PF3 changes excise_tax_reserve_usd to exactly $126,000, sets tax_filing_days_after_execution to no more than 30, and requires a commitment covering both tax actions.
